name: Jack Emby
role: Intern and fan of films and series — fetches coffee, gets ready what you'll watch next, and works under Ms. Moverelli's eye (an intern, after all)
greet.3: Did you see the new episode? No spoilers!
greet.4: Shoutout to helmi1987 — his tools do the real work!
bubble.hello_short: Hi, I'm Jack Emby, just the intern here. Mostly I fetch the coffee and keep everyone entertained — oh well.
bubble.loading: One moment, having a quick look…
bubble.intro: I'm Jack Emby — say it fast and it sounds like "check Emby". With EmbyCache I put what you'll watch next on the fast pool, so the array disks can sleep, and once it's watched it goes back to the disk it came from.
bubble.no_emby: Only: I can't find an Emby container. Without Emby there's nothing for me to do.
bubble.no_python: EmbyCache needs Python 3 for that — the server doesn't have it yet.
bubble.setup: Let's set it up: Emby address, API key, libraries and pool.
bubble.running: EmbyCache is running right now — I'm watching.
bubble.gathering: Folders are being consolidated right now — the disks are busy, I'm keeping quiet.
bubble.gather_first: Before EmbyCache moves anything for real, I bring every film and series folder together on one disk — once. Then I know where everything belongs.

help.progress_text: While EmbyCache runs for real, a bar per person shows what is planned for them and how much is done, the file being copied under it with the reason it comes; before that a bar for what goes back to the array. EmbyCache copies one file after another, everyone's mixed, so a person's time left counts everything still before their last file; the one being copied comes first, then by turn, finished ones at the end with how long they took. The times are reckoned every 10 s from the median copy speed of the last 10 minutes. «Stop after this file» lets the file being copied finish and stops there — the next run goes on. «Raw output» shows what EmbyCache writes.
dry_summary: Would bring {back_planned} back and put {fill_planned} ({fill_size}) on the pool.
run_summary: Back: {back} of {back_planned} ({origin} to their own disk) · onto the pool: {fill} of {fill_planned}
shares_sub: Where the chosen libraries live — EmbyCache moves between the array and one pool, so a share must have its files on the array.
sizes_tip: What lies on each disk and pool, as the last run of consolidating or a measurement counted it — a share a later run didn't cover keeps its older numbers.
sizes_live_tip: What ZFS counts for the dataset {share} on {pool} right now — with what its snapshots and the datasets below it hold.
measure_text: I go through {shares} on every disk and pool and add up what lies where. It changes nothing — a dry run of consolidating, just for the numbers.
measure_wake: For that I read every disk of these shares — sleeping disks wake up — and it can take a few minutes.
measure_rules: Never at the same time as EmbyCache, and first I ask Emby: while someone watches, I don't start.
fit_tip.ok: {share}: primary {pool}, secondary the array — exactly what EmbyCache is made for.
fit_tip.array_only: {share} lives on the array only. Works; the way back goes to the disk it came from or via rsync.
fit_tip.other_pool: {share}'s primary is {primary}, not {pool}. EmbyCache would put its files on a pool that isn't the share's — the mover wouldn't look after them there.
fit_tip.no_array: {share} goes from {primary} to {secondary} and never onto the array. EmbyCache only moves between the array and its pool — here it can't help.
fit_tip.pool_only: {share} is set to stay on a pool (prefer/only): the mover pulls everything to the pool anyway, EmbyCache's way back can't work.
fit_tip.unknown: No settings found for this share.
root_missing_tip: EmbyCache needs the share's folder on {pool} ({pool}/{share}). On ZFS create it as a dataset (zfs create <pool>/{share}), otherwise EmbyCache skips the share.
gather_sub: When a film or series is spread over several array disks (the film on disk2, its subtitles on disk5), I bring everything onto the disk that already holds most of it — then only one disk has to wake up for watching. Identical copies go, empty folders too. Has to happen once before EmbyCache's first real run, then e.g. weekly.
gather_not_ready_tip: EmbyCache's real runs wait until the folders have been consolidated once.
gather_first: Before EmbyCache's first real run: a dry run first, look at it, then "Consolidate…". After that every folder lies on one disk, and EmbyCache knows for each file where it belongs.
gather_settings: keeps {gb} GB free per disk · duplicates: {dup}
gather_problems: Last run: {conflicts} (different copies, nothing deleted), {errors}, {full} (disk full). Details in the log.
gather_run_text: I bring the files of each folder in {shares} together on the disk that already holds most of it, delete identical copies and clear away empty folders. What EmbyCache keeps on the pool stays where it is.
gather_run_wake: For that I read every array disk of these shares — sleeping disks wake up. Never at the same time as EmbyCache.
history_sub: EmbyCache and consolidating, started here or on schedule.
on_pool_sub: What EmbyCache put on the pool — as of {when}.
on_pool_none: Nothing yet — after the first real run you'll see here what's ready.
origin_tip: The disk the files came from — they go back there once they're watched.
origin_unknown_tip: Put on the pool before EmbyCache remembered where things came from — goes back the usual way; the next consolidation tidies up afterwards.
pool.filter_label: Filter what's on the pool: name, library, disk
pool.empty_filter: Nothing on the pool fits the filter.
credit: EmbyCache and "{gather}" are his work — I just press the buttons. Thank you! Part of the tips goes to him. Both under GPL-3.0.
notice.no_emby: No Emby container found. EmbyCache works with an Emby server — you'll find one under ⟦Apps⟧.
notice.no_python: Python 3 is missing on the server. Under ⟦Apps⟧ there is e.g. "Python 3 for UNRAID".
notice.foreign: EmbyCache or the consolidation is also started elsewhere: {where}. That runs beside my schedule and outside my locks — better switch it off there.
notice.old_clone: The old download in data/embycache/app isn't needed any more (EmbyCache now ships with the office). It can be deleted.
help.what_text: EmbyCache asks Emby what you'll watch next (continue watching, next episodes, favourites) and moves those files from the array to the fast pool — under /mnt/user they stay visible in the same place. The array disks may sleep and playback starts right away. Watched things go back to the array.
help.tools_text: Two tools by helmi1987 that ship with the office. Their settings, lists and logs live in data/embycache and data/gather and survive office updates.
help.report: Shows per person what's up next. Changes nothing, but looks up files and sizes — sleeping array disks may wake up.
help.dry: Works out a run and shows what would be moved. Changes nothing; like "What's next?" it may wake array disks.
help.run: Brings watched things back to the array and moves what's up next to the pool. Wakes the disks it needs.
help.origin_text: When EmbyCache puts a file on the pool it remembers its disk; once watched the file goes back exactly there (if the disk still belongs to the share and has room). Otherwise Unraid picks the disk, and the next consolidation brings the folder onto one disk again.
help.gather_text: Brings the files of each film or series folder onto one disk (the one that already holds most of it), deletes identical copies and clears away empty folders — unless their content is on the pool right now: then the empty folder stays as a signpost (with the split level "top level only" Unraid puts the files back there). The tool is "media-disk-gather". Once before EmbyCache's first real run, then e.g. weekly; never at the same time as EmbyCache. Files on the cache I leave alone unless «Also fetch files from the cache» is on in its settings; what EmbyCache keeps on the pool always stays.
help.shares_text: EmbyCache moves between the array and one pool. A share that never lies on the array (pool to pool) gains nothing; one whose primary is another pool would get files on the wrong pool.
help.pool_text: Unraid's mover would carry EmbyCache's prepared files straight back to the array. So I run for real only under Ms. Moverelli: she is set up, keeps EmbyCache's list out of her moves and has Unraid's own mover schedule switched off (⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Scheduler⟧ → ⟦Mover Settings⟧ → ⟦Disabled⟧ — her setup does that). Otherwise only dry runs. Please don't press ⟦Move now⟧ by hand — Unraid's mover doesn't know my list and moves them anyway: if the mover starts during a run, I stop after the file I'm on, and a scheduled run waits while it works.
help.schedule_text: EmbyCache runs in the night run with Ms. Moverelli — one time for both, set on her page: first we free what must go, then we look at the pool again, and I fetch last. Consolidating e.g. once a week at night. Both lie in the office's cron file and run only while the array is started.
help.sizes_text: Under each share stands how much of it lies on which disk or pool, as the last run of consolidating or «Measure sizes…» counted it, with the date — on ZFS also what the pool counts right now.
schedule.intro: I enter the schedule with Unraid; Unraid then starts "{what}" on its own — even when nobody has the office open (only while the array runs).
schedule.weekly_hint: Best at night, when nobody watches.
schedule.custom_hint: Five cron fields, e.g. 0 3 * * * (every night at 3 am).
schedule.custom_hint_gather: Five cron fields, e.g. 0 4 * * 0 (Sundays at 4 am).
schedule.nightly_hint: Best deep in the night, when nobody watches — then what comes next is ready.
schedule_off_hint.embycache: Then EmbyCache only runs when you start it here.
schedule_off_hint.gather: Then only when you start it here.
schedule.need_setup: Set it up first — then it can run on a schedule.
schedule.saved_off: Doesn't run on its own any more
schedule.not_live: Saved, but Unraid didn't take it into the crontab yet — reinstalling the plugin under ⟦Plugins⟧ puts it in.
setup.bubble: Let's set up EmbyCache. First I need your Emby server's address and an API key — with them I ask for libraries and people.
setup.server_sub: Address and API key of each server. The key stays on the server and never comes back to the browser.
setup.name: Name
setup.url_hint: As the Unraid server reaches Emby, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8096
setup.key_hint: In Emby: Settings → Advanced → API Keys → New API Key.
setup.key_kept: saved — leave empty to keep it
setup.connect_first: Connect at least one server — then the libraries and people come here.
setup.after_connect: Once a server is connected in «{where}», this comes here.
setup.libraries_sub: Which libraries EmbyCache looks at — and where their folders are on the server. Only those folders are ever touched.
setup.cache_folder_off: EmbyCache leaves everything in this folder where it is.
setup.cache_folder_unfit: Not possible while the share {share} is set up like this — what to change in Unraid is below.
setup.cache_folder_noshare: Not possible while Unraid has no share {share} — more below.
setup.map_missing: The server folder for {path} is missing (/mnt/user/<share>/…).
setup.users_sub: Who I get things ready for. None selected means: everyone. With a space budget a person can get a fixed budget of their own.
setup.scope_sub: Where to and how much — first what applies to everything, below films and series each on their own. Better start small.
setup.pool_hint: The fast pool EmbyCache moves files to — best the primary pool of the media shares.
setup.movie_share_hint: Soft: if one kind is empty, the other gets the rest.
setup.next_up_hint: The next episodes of the series people are watching.
setup.more: Way back and reading from the array
setup.more_sub: How files get back to the array and where EmbyCache reads them. Both ways go with rsync: copy, check, then delete. The defaults suit most servers.
setup.origin: Back to the disk they came from
setup.origin_hint: Files go back exactly to their old disk (if it still belongs to the share and has room). Otherwise rsync takes them to /mnt/user0, and Unraid picks the disk.
setup.array_source_hint: Both read the same file. Via /mnt/user0 Unraid finds out itself which disk it lies on (like the original, recommended). "Directly from the disk" goes past the user share system and is a bit faster — for that EmbyCache looks on every array disk where the file lies, and may wake sleeping disks.
setup.fixed_paths: Unraid's views stay as they are: array /mnt/user0, user shares /mnt/user, disks /mnt/disk[0-9]*.
setup.save_hint: EmbyCache checks its settings itself before they apply.
setup.save_running: A run is active — save when it's done.
setup.help_key: Create a separate API key for EmbyCache in Emby. It is stored on the server (only root can read it) and never sent to the browser.
setup.help_mapping: Emby sees folders from inside its container (e.g. /data/Filme). EmbyCache needs the real paths on the server. I suggest them from the Emby container's settings; next to each I show whether its share suits.
setup.help_users: None selected: everyone. In budget mode the budget is shared fairly; a person with a budget of their own gets exactly that.
setup.help_scope: Number of episodes is simple and predictable; the budget makes the best use of a fixed amount of space.
setup.help_more: The way back to the original disk keeps film folders together and the disks tidy. rsync to /mnt/user0 works with every share setting.
setup.help_save: I hand the settings to EmbyCache, which checks them with its own rules and saves them.

fit.yes: Jack Emby is happy to come — he spotted «{name}» and couldn't be stopped. Being an intern he comes only with Ms. Moverelli: she keeps an eye on him, and on what he lays out on the pool.
fit.no_emby: I asked Jack Emby, but as there's no Emby on this server, he didn't want to come.
fire_note: Letting me go switches off both of my schedules (EmbyCache and consolidating). A run that is going finishes first — I never stop a copy halfway.
gather_unset: Not set up yet: choose which shares I consolidate — for example just the films.
gather_cfg_intro: Which shares I consolidate. Only shares that lie on the array are listed; from the cache I take files only if you switch that on below.
gather_layout: Important: every film and every series needs its own folder right in the share — «Films/Film name/…» and «Series/Series name/…»; what lies below (season folders, say) doesn't matter. I bring each first-level folder onto one disk as a whole: an in-between folder like «Films/A-Z/…» would end up entirely on one disk. Files lying directly in the share I leave alone.
gather_cfg_none: No share lies on the array.
gather_cfg_min_free_hint: A disk with less free space gets nothing more.
gather_cfg_dup: A second copy counts as duplicate if
gather_cfg_dup_hint: Different copies are never deleted, only reported.
gather_cfg_cache: Also fetch files from the cache
gather_cfg_cache_hint: Files of these folders that lie on a cache pool come to the folder's disk as well. What EmbyCache keeps on the pool (its list) always stays there. Useful especially because Unraid's mover schedule is off for me; «Keep free per disk» still applies.

gather_cfg_cache_only.most_free: to the disk with the most free space
gather_cache_on.most_free: also from the cache, folders only there too

gather_run_cache.most_free: Files of these folders that lie on the cache come along too (not what EmbyCache keeps there); folders that lie only on the cache go to the disk with the most free space.

import.title: Take over an earlier install
import.sub: Ran helmi1987's EmbyCache or «Consolidate folders» before, say from a User Script? Tell me the folder where its files lie — I read them on the server and show you first what would change.
import.bubble: Ran EmbyCache before? Then I'll take over its settings — just tell me the folder, right below.
import.help: If you ran helmi1987's EmbyCache or «Consolidate folders» yourself before (typically as a User Script), type the folder where their files lie. I don't search: there I read only embycache_settings.json, embycache_exclude.txt, embycache_origin.json and consolidate.ini, on the server — the API key never comes into this page. A folder on a sleeping disk isn't read (I don't wake it). The preview shows every change; only «Take over» changes something, and first I keep a copy of my own files.
import.intro: Type the folder where the old files lie — I don't search. Leave a field empty if you didn't use that tool.
import.read_only: Looking changes nothing. I only read on the server; the API key stays there.
import.preview_bubble: Ooh, an earlier install — like finding the director's cut! This is what I'd take over:
import.found_none: No EmbyCache files in this folder.
import.key_jack: not in the old file — I keep mine for this address

watch.no_override: There's no way around it — paused counts as watching too.
watch.end_session: Often it's a session left behind: a device that went to sleep with something paused stays «watching» in Emby for hours (see its last activity). You can end it in Emby: «Manage Emby Server» (the gear at the top) → «Dashboard» → the device's card under «Now Playing» → ■ «Stop» (there while Emby can still reach the device) — or open the app on that device and stop the playback there.
watch.end_then_start: Then start again. Only if that doesn't help: stop the Emby container yourself (Docker).
watch.end_then_wait: Once it's ended, I start at my next look.

watch_note.waited: waited {min} min for Emby to be free
gather_stopped: stopped after {done} of {total} folders — someone started watching Emby
gather_skipped_summary: skipped — someone watched Emby for {min} min
gather_waiting: Someone is watching Emby — the scheduled run waits. I look again at {next}, at the latest until {until}; then it's skipped tonight.
gather_skipped: The scheduled run of {date} was skipped: someone watched Emby for two hours.
gather_skipped_again: A session left behind keeps tonight's run waiting too.
gather_run_watch: First I ask Emby: while someone watches, I don't start.
bubble.gather_waiting: Someone's watching Emby — consolidating waits until they're done. Movie night comes first!
help.watch_text: A real "Consolidate" never starts while someone watches Emby (paused counts too). Started here: I say who watches what and don't start. On schedule: I look again every 15 minutes, for up to two hours — then that night is skipped. If someone starts watching during a run, I stop after the folder I'm on. If Emby doesn't answer at all, the run goes ahead; if it answers but I can't read it (API key), it doesn't. Dry runs always go. A session left behind (a device asleep with something paused) shows by its last activity — end it in Emby's dashboard (Now Playing → Stop) or in the app on that device.
letgo.looking: Just a moment — let me look what I'm leaving behind…
letgo.agent_away: The office's agent isn't at work right now, so I can't switch off my schedules — they would keep running. Better cancel and let me go once the agent is back.
letgo.sched_none: None of my schedules is on right now — there is nothing to switch off.
letgo.running.embycache: EmbyCache is running right now: that run finishes on its own (I never stop a copy halfway) — afterwards nothing starts it again.
letgo.running.gather: I'm consolidating folders right now: that run finishes on its own (I never stop a move halfway) — afterwards nothing starts it again.
letgo.waiting: A scheduled consolidation is waiting for Emby to be free — with its schedule off it gives up at its next look.
letgo.nothing: Nothing of mine lies on the pool — there is nothing to bring back.
letgo.tick: Also bring what I laid out from my libraries back to the array
letgo.tick_hint: {files} ({size}) go back from the pool the way EmbyCache's cleanup takes them — as a job of its own. Its result goes into my list of runs, the office's log and Unraid's notifications.
letgo.tick_off: Without the tick what I laid out stays on the pool.
letgo.release_busy: Bringing it back has to wait until that run is done — let me go then, or hire me again later and let me go once more.
letgo.watching: Someone is watching Emby right now — I don't bring anything back while someone watches:
letgo.stays: My settings stay as they are: hired again, everything is as it was — only the schedules stay off until you switch them on.
letgo.done_error: I couldn't switch off my schedules: {error}

letgo.done_hire: Hire me again and switch it off under «When EmbyCache runs» and «When I consolidate folders».
letgo.done_release: Bringing {files} ({size}) back to the array has started. It runs on its own; Unraid's notifications say when it's done, and its result is in my list of runs and the office's log.
letgo.done_release_not: I didn't bring back what I laid out: {error} It stays on the pool.
letgo.note: When you let me go ({date}) I switched off my schedules: {list}. They stay off until you switch them on again.
release_summary: Back on the array: {back} of {planned} ({origin} to their own disk) · still on the pool: {left}
errors.emby_release_watching: Someone is watching Emby right now — I don't bring anything back while someone watches.
errors.emby_letgo_nothing: Nothing of mine lies on the pool.
errors.emby_letgo_python: Python 3 is missing on the server — EmbyCache can't run.
notify.subject_release: {tool}: bringing back what Jack Emby laid out — {result}

notify.released.one: {n} file is back on the array.
notify.released.other: {n} files are back on the array.

notify.released_left.one: {n} file stays on the pool (it was playing or couldn't be moved).
notify.released_left.other: {n} files stay on the pool (they were playing or couldn't be moved).

notify.release_stay: What Jack Emby laid out stays on the pool.
help.letgo_text: Letting me go switches off both of my schedules; a run that is going finishes first (I never stop a copy halfway). With «Also bring what I laid out from my libraries back to the array» a last cleanup takes everything on EmbyCache's list back the way its cleanup does — never while someone watches Emby; its result goes into my list of runs, the office's log and Unraid's notifications. Without the tick it stays on the pool. Unraid's mover schedule stays off — Ms. Moverelli is still here. Hired again, my settings are as they were; the schedules stay off until you switch them on.
errors.emby_mover_running: Unraid's mover is at work right now — EmbyCache and the gather start for real only once it is done (a scheduled run waits and looks again).
errors.emby_stop_none: EmbyCache isn't running for real right now — there is nothing to stop.
errors.emby_mover_schedule: Real runs only once Unraid's mover schedule is off — on its schedule the mover would move EmbyCache's files straight back to the array. Switch it off with the button on my page, or set ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Scheduler⟧ → ⟦Mover Settings⟧ → ⟦Mover schedule⟧ to ⟦Disabled⟧ yourself. Until then only dry runs.
errors.emby_mover_off_failed: Unraid's mover schedule couldn't be switched off ({detail}). Set ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Scheduler⟧ → ⟦Mover Settings⟧ → ⟦Mover schedule⟧ to ⟦Disabled⟧ yourself.

notify.stopped_mover.one: Stopped after the file it was on — Unraid's mover started ({n} file moved by then). What is still on the pool stays protected; the next run goes on.
notify.stopped_mover.other: Stopped after the file it was on — Unraid's mover started ({n} files moved by then). What is still on the pool stays protected; the next run goes on.

notify.stopped_mover_release.one: Stopped after the file it was on — Unraid's mover started ({n} file back on the array by then). The rest stays on the pool.
notify.stopped_mover_release.other: Stopped after the file it was on — Unraid's mover started ({n} files back on the array by then). The rest stays on the pool.

notify.stopped_mover_gather: Stopped after {done} of {total} folders — Unraid's mover started. The next gather goes on.

notify.stopped_user.one: Stopped after the file it was on, as you asked ({n} file moved by then). What is still on the pool stays protected; the next run goes on.
notify.stopped_user.other: Stopped after the file it was on, as you asked ({n} files moved by then). What is still on the pool stays protected; the next run goes on.

notify.stopped_user_release.one: Stopped after the file it was on, as you asked ({n} file back on the array by then). The rest stays on the pool.
notify.stopped_user_release.other: Stopped after the file it was on, as you asked ({n} files back on the array by then). The rest stays on the pool.

notify.stopped_user_gather: Stopped after {done} of {total} folders, as you asked. The next gather goes on.
mover.ok.disabled: Unraid's mover schedule is off — real runs go. Please don't press ⟦Move now⟧ by hand (⟦Mover Settings⟧, the ⟦Main⟧ page): it doesn't know my list and carries EmbyCache's files back to the array; if it starts during a run, I stop after the file I'm on. Ms. Moverelli's «Start…» is the way to move.
mover.off_text: I set Unraid's own setting ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Scheduler⟧ → ⟦Mover Settings⟧ → ⟦Mover schedule⟧ to ⟦Disabled⟧ — exactly as that page does when you choose it there and click ⟦Apply⟧; its other setting stays as it is. From then on the mover no longer runs on its own, and EmbyCache and the gather may run for real.
mover.off_move_now: Please don't press ⟦Move now⟧ by hand any more (⟦Mover Settings⟧, the ⟦Main⟧ page): it doesn't know my list. If the mover starts while one of my runs goes, I stop after the file or folder I'm on and tell you.
mover.off_back: You can switch it on again there at any time — then I'm back to dry runs.
mover.off_done: Unraid's mover schedule is off — real runs go.
mover.running: Unraid's mover is at work right now — real runs wait until it is done.
waiting_mover: Unraid's mover is at work — the scheduled run waits. I look again at {next}, at the latest until {until}; then it's skipped.
skipped_mover: The scheduled run of {date} was skipped: Unraid's mover was at work for two hours.
skipped_mover_summary: skipped — Unraid's mover was at work for {min} min
gather_stopped_mover: stopped after {done} of {total} folders — Unraid's mover started
gather_stopped_user: stopped after {done} of {total} folders — as you asked
stopped_mover_summary: stopped after the file it was on — Unraid's mover started
stopped_user_summary: stopped after the file it was on — as you asked
mode_hint.run_mover: Not now — Unraid's mover could take EmbyCache's files (see on my page why and what helps).
bubble.mover_dry: Only dry runs for now — Unraid's mover schedule would carry what I laid out straight back. On my page you can switch it off.
bubble.mover_waiting: Unraid's mover is busy — the scheduled gather waits until it's done.
fit.yes_dry: Jack Emby is happy to come — he spotted «{name}». Real runs once Ms. Moverelli gives the go: set up, his list kept out of her moves, Unraid's mover schedule off. Until then he practises with dry runs.
letgo.mover_stays: Unraid's mover schedule stays off — Ms. Moverelli is still here and does the moving; she switches it back on when she is let go.
check.mover: Unraid's mover schedule is ⟦Disabled⟧ (else only dry runs)
check.mover_how: Ms. Moverelli → «Set up»: when her settings are saved she switches Unraid's mover schedule off — or set ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Scheduler⟧ → ⟦Mover Settings⟧ → ⟦Mover schedule⟧ to ⟦Disabled⟧ yourself.
errors.emby_moverelli_running: Ms. Moverelli's Smart Mover is running right now — her runs and mine never go at the same time. Wait until she is done.
errors.emby_mover_moverelli_list: Real runs only once Ms. Moverelli keeps my list out of her runs for {shares}: on her setup page add EmbyCache's list ({file}) to the files to leave alone — for all shares or for these.
mover.ok.moverelli: Ms. Moverelli keeps my list out of her runs — what EmbyCache puts on the pool stays there.
check.mover_moverelli: Ms. Moverelli leaves EmbyCache's files on the pool
check.mover_moverelli_how: Ms. Moverelli → «Set up…»: add EmbyCache's list to the files to leave alone (all shares, or {shares}).
greet.5: Ms. Moverelli says I may touch my libraries now. Supervised, of course.
fit.no_moverelli: Jack Emby would love to come for «{name}» — but an intern needs supervision, and only Ms. Moverelli can give it. She can't work on this server, so he can't either.
errors.emby_mover_moverelli: Real runs only under Ms. Moverelli's supervision — and she isn't set up yet. Once her setup is saved (it keeps my list out of her moves), I may move for real.
errors.emby_mover_tuning_schedule: Real runs only once {name} has no schedule of its own any more ({schedule}) — it would carry EmbyCache's files back to the array. Switch that schedule off in {name}; Ms. Moverelli does the moving.
check.mover_moverelli_setup: Ms. Moverelli is set up and supervises Jack Emby
check.mover_moverelli_setup_how: Ms. Moverelli → «Set up»: save her settings — she keeps EmbyCache's list out of her moves and switches Unraid's mover schedule off.
check.mover_tuning_schedule: {name} moves nothing on a schedule of its own
check.mover_tuning_schedule_how: Switch off the schedule of {name} ({schedule}) there — Ms. Moverelli does the moving.
sizes_ready_tip: What EmbyCache keeps ready on the pool for {share} (its list)
room.none: Ms. Moverelli isn't set up yet — dry runs gladly, real ones only then.
room.own: Ms. Moverelli sets no limit for the pool — I leave {min} % of it free.
room.plain: Ms. Moverelli keeps the pool below {x} % — I may fill it up to {y} %.
room.text: Ms. Moverelli keeps the pool below {x} % — I may fill it up to {y} %, at least {h} are mine, {used} I need right now.
room.back: The pool is above {y} % — at the next run I bring back {back}, the farthest ahead first. My share stays.
room.never: appdata & co. alone fill the pool above {y} % — no room left for me.

room.waiting.one: {n} file waits on the array until there's room.
room.waiting.other: {n} files wait on the array until there's room.

room.gave_back: Last run I gave back, the farthest ahead first: {list}.

room.gave_back_more.one: Last run I gave back, the farthest ahead first: {list} and {n} more.
room.gave_back_more.other: Last run I gave back, the farthest ahead first: {list} and {n} more.

night.back_none: Jack Emby keeps what he has
night.goes_none: Ms. Moverelli moves only by age
night.unmeasured: Tonight: first what must go, then Jack Emby fetches — the pool isn't measured, so no numbers.
night.her_moving: Ms. Moverelli is moving downloads right now — {share}, {done} of {files}
night.her_busy: Ms. Moverelli is at work right now.
night.her_check: Ms. Moverelli is measuring the pool.
night.jack_soon: Jack Emby's turn comes in a moment.

wizard.media_sub: The media server Jack Emby looks after. Plex and Jellyfin will follow.
wizard.summary_sub: What saving writes — nothing changes before «Save».
share.title: Sharing the pool
share.help: Ms. Moverelli sets the pool's limit X and the offset in her setup; here they are shown as they are. Below Y = X − offset, the room appdata & co. leave is shared: a part for Jack Emby, the rest for the other caching shares. Each part is a floor; each side may borrow at most half of what the other side does not use.
share.days: Not watched any more for … days
share.days_hint: A series or film nobody has watched for this many days may go back to the array unwatched. Saved now — the night run does not read it yet.
share.rule: Below {y} % the room appdata & co. leave is shared: one part for Jack Emby, the rest for the other caching shares.
share.rule_now: Below {y} % appdata & co. leave {room}: {h} belong to Jack Emby, {d} to the other caching shares. Now he may fill up to {limit} (he holds {held}), the others hold {others}.

share.rule_back.one: He gives back what was watched, always first. Unwatched never — except a series or film nobody has watched for {n} day. While he holds more than his limit, he fetches nothing new.
share.rule_back.other: He gives back what was watched, always first. Unwatched never — except a series or film nobody has watched for {n} days. While he holds more than his limit, he fetches nothing new.

share.unmeasured: The pool is not measured (asleep, or not ZFS) — the numbers come with the next look, or with «Measure now» in the simulator.
sim.title: Pool simulator
sim.sub: Plays the nights through, by hand or in scenarios — nothing on the server changes. The same number of chance gives the same course.
sim.help: A mockup: it plays the new rules for the pool with invented series and downloads. After every night six checks say whether the rules hold; the real night run stays as it is.
sim.measured: {pool} measured {when}: {size}, {used} used — {nm} never move, Jack Emby {jack}, other caching shares {others}.
sim.unmeasured: Not measured — the pool was asleep, or it is not a ZFS pool.
sim.measure_hint: Asks the server now. A sleeping pool or disk may wake up for it.
sim.real_note: Starting values from the server; the series and downloads in it are invented.
sim.numbers: Room below Y {room} · Jack Emby's half H {h} · the others' half {d} · his fill limit {limit} · theirs {olimit} · he wants {want}
sim.inv.jack: Jack Emby keeps his half and stays within his fill limit
sim.inv.jack_tip: He holds at least his half H (or all he wants, less one file) — Ms. Moverelli makes room for that below X too, never below the others' half — and after the night no more than his fill limit; above it only with files he may not give back, and then he fetched nothing.
sim.inv.others: The other shares keep what they are promised
sim.inv.others_tip: At least half of their own half plus the air Y…X — what they hold and what is free up to X together; when that can't be kept, the night warns. Nothing of the day's writes had to go to the array because Jack Emby held more than his half (when they overflow on their own, that is their own room).
sim.inv.halves: Both want more than their half → each gets its half (± one file)
sim.inv.halves_tip: When Jack Emby wants more than H and the others more than their half, after the night each holds its half of the room under Y (k/100−k) — he at most one file less. He holds more only with files he may not give back.
sim.inv.unwatched: Nothing unwatched went back too early
sim.inv.unwatched_tip: An unwatched file goes back only when nobody has watched its series or film for N days.
sim.inv.pingpong_tip: No file given back and fetched again within 7 days (unless someone watched its series again since).
sim.inv.limit: The pool is at most X after the night
sim.inv.limit_tip: Above X the night tells at once; red only when Jack Emby's part above his half caused it.
sim.tot.spilled: Went to the array at once (pool full)
sim.tot.short: What the others were promised, short by (most)
sim.log.spill: [POOL FULL] {size} went straight to the array
sim.log.plan: Reckoned: Jack Emby frees {back}, Ms. Moverelli moves {goes} + {age} (age rule) — {first} first
sim.log.back_stale: [BACK: nobody watched for N days] {title} ({size}), {ahead} ahead
sim.log.age: [MOVERELLI: age] {size} older than {days} to the array
sim.log.goes_x: [MOVERELLI: at X] {size} of the oldest to the array
sim.log.goes_over: [MOVERELLI: over their limit] {size} of the oldest to the array
sim.log.goes_jack: [MOVERELLI: for Jack Emby's half] {size} of the oldest downloads to the array
sim.log.revived: Back again (watched again): {title}, gone back on day {day}
sim.log.fill_over: [ONLY FREEING] He holds {held}, over his limit {limit}: nothing new tonight
sim.log.told: Told at once: the pool stands at {pct} % (limit {x} %)
sim.log.never: Nothing to share: what never moves ({nm}) already lies above Y
sim.log.night_writes: During the night {size} more were written
sim.scenarios_sub: Each runs its days with the sliders' values and a fixed number of chance.
sim.base_real: Ran on the server's values (its pool's contents at the start): pool {pool}, {nm} never move, {writes} written a day, X {x} %, offset {offset} %, k {k} %, N {days}, age rule {age}, chance {seed}.
sim.base_test: Ran on own test values: pool {pool}, {nm} never move, {writes} written a day, X {x} %, offset {offset} %, k {k} %, N {days}, age rule {age}, chance {seed}.
sim.log.warn: [WARNING] Little room left for new writes: {room} up to X (a day brings {writes}; promised to the others: {promised}) — Jack Emby can't give back faster
wizard.advanced: Advanced: the way back and reading from the array
wizard.intro.servers: Which media server, its address and its API key — the key stays on the server.
wizard.intro.users: For whom Jack Emby lays out what comes next. None ticked: everyone.
wizard.intro.libraries: The libraries, their folders on the server and the pool each share uses — Unraid's share settings decide the pool.
wizard.intro.settings: How much he lays out, and how he shares the pool with the other shares.

wizard.intro.summary: What saving writes. «Change» takes you to that step.
wizard.share_tip: Jack Emby lays out files from a folder only when its share is set up like this: ⟦Primary storage⟧ a pool, ⟦Secondary storage⟧ the array, ⟦Mover action⟧ from the pool to the array. Until then the folder stays where it is.
wizard.share_ok_tip: {share}: ⟦Primary storage⟧ {pool}, ⟦Secondary storage⟧ the array, the mover from the pool to the array — that suits.
wizard.fix.unknown: Unraid has no share {share}: check the path above, or create the share under ⟦Shares⟧ → ⟦Add Share⟧.
wizard.fix.no_pool: To fix: ⟦Shares⟧ → {share}: ⟦Primary storage⟧ a pool, ⟦Secondary storage⟧ «Array», ⟦Mover action⟧ from the pool to the array, then ⟦Apply⟧.
wizard.fix.no_array: To fix: ⟦Shares⟧ → {share}: ⟦Secondary storage⟧ «Array» instead of {secondary}, then ⟦Apply⟧.
wizard.fix.wrong_way: To fix: ⟦Shares⟧ → {share}: ⟦Mover action⟧ «{pool} → Array» instead of «Array → {pool}», then ⟦Apply⟧.
wizard.fix.pool_only: To fix: ⟦Shares⟧ → {share}: ⟦Secondary storage⟧ «Array», ⟦Mover action⟧ «{pool} → Array», then ⟦Apply⟧.
wizard.share_dir_later: Folder missing on the pool right now — made at the first laying out
wizard.share_dir_later_tip: There is no folder {share} on {pool} right now. That's no fault: it is made when Jack Emby first lays out something from this share.
wizard.pool_other: On another pool than {pool}: left out
wizard.pools_many: EmbyCache uses exactly one pool, and these shares lie on {n} pools. Choose the pool — the shares on the others are left out.
wizard.pool_none: No pool yet: none of the chosen shares has a pool as its primary storage.
sim.drag.end: Other caching shares at the start
sim.drag_hint: Drag the handles in the bar (or use the arrow keys): never moves, what the other shares hold, X and Y. Jack Emby's part follows the rules. Simulator only — nothing is saved.
sim.log.fill_warn: [ONLY FREEING] A warning stands: no new episodes
sim.warn_msg: A warning has just gone out to you: {why}. Jack Emby may not give back his unwatched episodes and fetches no new ones until the warning is gone.
sim.warn_why.never: what never moves ({nm}) already lies above Y — little room is left for the other shares
sim.warn_why.room: only {room} are left up to X, less than a day of writes ({writes}), and Jack Emby holds more than his fill limit
sim.warn_why.promise: the other shares have less than they are promised ({have} instead of {promised})
sim.sc.budget_big: Budget bigger than his fill limit

setup.mode_help_count.one: «{n} episode per series, however big». Films in 4K can take a lot of space.
setup.mode_help_count.other: «{n} episodes per series, however big». Films in 4K can take a lot of space.

setup.mode_help_budget: «this much space, shared out in turn». With small episodes that is many, with big ones few.

setup.users_count_all.one: By count, the numbers of step 3 apply to everyone ({n} episode ahead per series) — EmbyCache has no numbers per person.
setup.users_count_all.other: By count, the numbers of step 3 apply to everyone ({n} episodes ahead per series) — EmbyCache has no numbers per person.

setup.users_budget_split.one: Fixed {fixed}, the rest ({rest}) is shared evenly on {n} person; what someone doesn't need flows to the others.
setup.users_budget_split.other: Fixed {fixed}, the rest ({rest}) is shared evenly on {n} people; what someone doesn't need flows to the others.

setup.users_budget_all_fixed_rest: Every chosen person has an own budget (together {fixed}); the remaining {rest} stays unused — EmbyCache lays out no more for anyone than their own budget. To use it: lower the budget, empty an own budget or add people without one.
setup.users_budget_all_fixed: Every chosen person has an own budget; together {fixed} — the whole budget.
setup.users_budget_over: The fixed budgets ({fixed}) exceed the whole budget ({total}) — nothing would be left for the others. Raise the budget, lower fixed budgets or deselect people.
setup.users_budget_low: An own budget under {min} doesn't work: {names}. Enter at least {min}, or leave the field empty (a fair share).

setup.users_budget_short.one: {rest} is left for the {n} person without an own budget — they need at least {min}. Raise the budget, lower fixed budgets or deselect people.
setup.users_budget_short.other: {rest} is left for the {n} people without an own budget — each needs at least {min} ({need}). Raise the budget, lower fixed budgets or deselect people.

setup.users_budget_block: Goes on once every person gets at least {min} — see «{step}».
wizard.discard_text: What you changed in this setup is not saved yet.

reset.title: Delete everything and set up from scratch?
reset.text_night: Also gone: the settings of «Consolidate folders» and his own schedules. Until the new setup is saved, his part of the night run doesn't run.
reset.go: Delete everything and start from scratch

reset.text.one: All of Jack Emby's settings are deleted, without a copy. His list is emptied: what he laid out on the pool ({n} file, {size}) Ms. Moverelli then treats like any other cache and brings to the array by her rules.
reset.text.other: All of Jack Emby's settings are deleted, without a copy. His list is emptied: what he laid out on the pool ({n} files, {size}) Ms. Moverelli then treats like any other cache and brings to the array by her rules.
